daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The National Police Chief installed six new regional police chiefs and appointed Irjen Wibowo as Traffic Corps Chief, replacing Irjen Agus Suryonugroho in a major reshuffle of the police leadership. The appointments signal a reorganization of police command structures across multiple regions. Separately, the presidential palace reiterated that law enforcement will be applied without favoritism in the corruption investigation into the free nutritious meals (MBG) program.

  • Democratic Party chairman AHY opened public voting for the party's 25th anniversary logo with prizes offered to participants.
  • The Kuansing regent's envelope of money for Environment and Forestry Minister Raja Juli was revealed by the KPK to have originated from a specific source, while the KPK stated that Raja Juli should have reported the envelope left by the regent.
  • Prabowo's younger sibling affirmed the MBG program will continue despite the corruption allegations.
  • The Defense Ministry issued a clarification after photos of Lt. Gen. Tri Budi Utomo appeared in news reports about the MBG corruption case.
  • Bali Governor Wayan Koster denied obstructing the free nutritious meals program.
  • MPR Deputy Speaker Bamsoet said Articles 45-49 of the Criminal Code strengthen corporate accountability.
  • The Polda Metro Jaya responded to Roy Suryo's pretrial motion.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia's ambassador to Iran represented the nation at the funeral of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, as world leaders paid their final respects. The Indonesian envoy's attendance marked Jakarta's diplomatic engagement with the new Iranian leadership following Khamenei's death. Meanwhile, the TNI announced plans to increase security deployment in vulnerable areas of Papua to address ongoing security challenges.

  • Indonesia and Russia joined forces to strengthen drug eradication efforts in Bali.
  • The US Embassy assisted in repatriating a pilot's body to Jakarta.
  • Indonesia urged stronger Asia-Pacific climate action at the UNESCAP forum.
  • The number of Indonesian workers trapped in online scam operations in Cambodia requesting repatriation has risen to 12,019.

Other

Indonesia and Meta launched a joint team to combat online gambling spam, with a minister warning of AI-driven gambling spam campaigns. An expert stated that the government-Meta joint team is key to tackling the problem. This initiative comes as the government intensifies its crackdown on illegal online gambling operations affecting Indonesian users.

  • A foreign national who purchased subsidized fuel was fined Rp 88 million.
  • An economist compared Indonesia and Vietnam, both now upper-middle-income countries.
  • Indonesia aims to become an ATMP hub for the Asia-Pacific region.
  • The Hajj Minister acknowledged that services in Mina were the weakest point of the 2026 hajj and requested a total evaluation, while also considering multi-story tents to address overcrowding and noting that pilgrim death rates have fallen but remain too high.
  • The cost of hajj in 2027 is predicted to rise due to rupiah weakness and aviation fuel price increases.
  • SalamAir opened a Muscat-Medan route, with the government optimistic it will boost Middle Eastern tourist arrivals.
